Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Problem, Review, then six stages, one question each.
  • Tab and own window read the simulator; link and HTML file do not.
  • Workshop: starred sub-steps only. Full: every sub-step.
  • Cases, tags, PFD, P&ID and fishbone branches come preloaded.
2

Part 2 · Stage by stage

What do I fill at each stage, and where does the OTS feed it?

Part 2 · the plan

From symptom to verified fix

  1. Engage and Defineurgency, IS / IS NOT, a measurable goal
  2. Explorefishbone, hypotheses, S/D/N screening
  3. Plantests that separate causes, and their cost
  4. The OTS feedslive pulls in the tab, CSV elsewhere
  5. Do it and Look backactual against predicted, then lessons

Stage 1 · Engage

First ask: is it time-critical?

  • Rate safety, environment, equipment, production.
  • Decide: run, safe-park or shut down.
  • Set your time budget.

Stage 2 · Define

IS / IS NOT draws the edge of the problem

  • What, where, when, extent: IS beside IS NOT.
  • The difference points at the cause.
  • Then a SMARTS goal with numbers.

Stage 3 · Explore

Every cause on the fishbone, then as a hypothesis

  • Six branches written for this unit.
  • Each idea: "if … then we should observe …".
  • Name what would kill it.

Interactive · click a cell to change S, D or N

Screen the hypotheses on evidence you already have

One D (denies) on firm evidence kills a hypothesis; only the survivors earn a plant test.

Stage 4 · Plan

Each test says what it can tell apart

  • Targets: the hypotheses it separates.
  • Prediction per hypothesis, before the test.
  • Kill rule, stop rule, way back.

Interactive · pick the tests to run

Cheap, safe and decisive comes first

For TE-1, USD 90 of sampling and looking leaves one hypothesis standing before any plant move.

OTS data & evidence page

From this OTS (live): three pulls, one click

  • Run data: every DCS trend.
  • Tag snapshot: now against design.
  • Event log, without hidden-fault lines.
  • Standalone copies: Data export CSV, then drop here.

Stages 5 and 6

Predict first, then compare with what happened

  • Record each test result and verdict.
  • Fix: predicted against actual tags.
  • Look back: prevent, check new hazards, lessons.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Engage before diagnosing; IS / IS NOT before causes.
  • Screen hypotheses with S/D/N; test only the survivors.
  • Order tests by cost and how much they separate.
  • Pull run, snapshot and log live; elsewhere use the CSV.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • TE-1 loads from Worked examples, never on its own.
  • Its evidence comes from three real OTS runs.
  • Lab and field tests left one hypothesis; the step confirmed it.
  • Hand in the .woods.json; the report and slides follow from it.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Work in the tab or own window so the simulator feeds you.

2

Finish every starred sub-step before moving on.

3

Screen with S/D/N, then test only the survivors.

4

Write the prediction before the test, then compare.

5

Save the .woods.json often; it is your hand-in.
